title: Treat context as a finite attention budget; spend it on the smallest high-signal set
statement: Curate the context window as a finite attention budget: find the smallest set of high-signal tokens that produce the desired behavior, rather than stuffing in everything that might be relevant, because recall degrades as the window fills (context rot).
rationale: Transformer attention creates n-squared pairwise relationships, so every added token dilutes focus. More context is not monotonically better; beyond a point it reduces reliable recall.
applies_when: Prompts or histories are growing over time
not_when: A short single-shot task well within the model's comfortable window
how: Prefer minimal, high-signal system prompts at the right altitude (neither brittle hardcoded logic nor vague guidance)
Use a small, curated set of canonical examples rather than an exhaustive edge-case list
Prune tool results and stale history that no longer inform the next decision
check: Is anything in the current context there because it MIGHT be relevant rather than because it is high-signal for the next step? That is budget you are wasting.
failure_if_absent: Long-running agents lose focus and recall as the window fills, and quality degrades in ways that look random.

evidence.title: Anthropic - Effective context engineering for AI agents
evidence.quote: Context, therefore, must be treated as a finite resource with diminishing marginal returns
evidence.note: Same post introduces context rot: recall decreases as token count rises.
